---
title: Receive vendor webhooks
description: Give a vendor an address on your instance to post webhooks to, then check each delivery came from the vendor, act on it and mark it handled.
---

With an endpoint on your instance, a connector can act on a vendor's webhook at once instead of waiting for its next scheduled read. Marfa stores each delivery as it arrived and answers the vendor; the connector does the rest. The examples follow a recipe box connector with a key of its own.

## With the kit

A connector built on [the connector kit](/build/connector) needs only [the endpoint](#create-an-endpoint) and an `inbound` section. The kit reads the deliveries, checks them and marks them:

```ts title="src/main.ts"
inbound: {
  verify: (delivery, env) =>
    verifyHmac({
      secret: env.RECIPES_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
      body: delivery.body,
      signature: delivery.header("X-Signature"),
      prefix: "sha256=",
    }),
  hints: () => "everything",
},
```

- **`verify`** says whether a delivery came from the vendor, here with the kit's `verifyHmac`. Declare the secret in `env` as a `secret`.
- **`hints`** says what the delivery tells the connector changed. `"everything"` makes the next run read the vendor whole.

Each run collects up to 500 deliveries, and a scheduled connector also looks for more between runs. The run's report counts those processed, rejected and duplicate. The [kit's README](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa-connectors/blob/main/template/README.md#receiving-webhooks) describes `inbound` in full.

## On the API

These are the operations underneath, for a connector built directly on the API. In the TypeScript examples, `marfa` is a [TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk) client made with the connector's key, and `connectorId` is the registration's ID.

### Create an endpoint

[Create an inbound endpoint](/reference/api/inbound-webhooks/createInboundEndpoint) makes a private address on your instance for the vendor to post to, usually once, by hand:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa connectors endpoints create 01a1f12f-798c-70d4-b57b-d57feabdad99 \
  --label "recipe box webhooks" --duplicate-header X-Delivery-Id
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /connectors/01a1f12f-798c-70d4-b57b-d57feabdad99/endpoints
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{ "label": "recipe box webhooks", "duplicate_header": "X-Delivery-Id" }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.POST("/connectors/{id}/endpoints", {
  params: { path: { id: connectorId } },
  body: { label: "recipe box webhooks", duplicate_header: "X-Delivery-Id" },
});
```

```json title="Response" status="201"
{
  "id": "01a1f133-2dc4-75cf-84fd-eb21a8a270fe",
  "connector_id": "01a1f12f-798c-70d4-b57b-d57feabdad99",
  "label": "recipe box webhooks",
  "duplicate_header": "x-delivery-id",
  "path": "/inbound/PLPN1aDOk55XjNqHkHKfSD-8a9SoehUsbTvSU_dhEGM",
  "created_at": "2026-11-19T00:27:05.540Z",
  "retired_at": null
}
```

- **Save the `path`.** The vendor posts without a credential, so the address is the secret. Only this answer shows it in full; later reads show `/inbound/****` and its last four characters.
- **Give the vendor the address:** your instance's public [address](/run/address) followed by the `path`. The `url` the CLI prints uses the address the CLI reaches your instance on, so check that the vendor can reach it too.
- **Keep the vendor's signing secret in the connector's settings.** Marfa never holds it.
- **`duplicate_header`** names the header that identifies a delivery, such as `X-GitHub-Delivery`, so Marfa can point out one the vendor sends twice.

### Read the deliveries

[List inbound deliveries](/reference/api/inbound-webhooks/listInboundDeliveries) answers the deliveries not yet handled, oldest first, without their bodies. `state=handled` or `state=any` reads the others, and `endpoint_id` limits the list to one endpoint:

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
GET /connectors/01a1f12f-798c-70d4-b57b-d57feabdad99/deliveries
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data: page } = await marfa.GET("/connectors/{id}/deliveries", {
  params: { path: { id: connectorId } },
});
```

Each delivery is the request as it arrived:

```json title="A delivery"
{
  "id": "01a1f133-2e4a-7567-a309-bb4fb58ba295",
  "endpoint_id": "01a1f133-2dc4-75cf-84fd-eb21a8a270fe",
  "received_at": "2026-11-19T00:27:05.674Z",
  "method": "POST",
  "query": "",
  "headers": [
    ["content-type", "application/json"],
    ["x-delivery-id", "d-100"],
    ["x-signature", "sha256=3dca2ba66de6139cbc7adca0d6a04a735ccf40ffdb37296ca389fe6c811e6c54"]
  ],
  "size": 18,
  "sha256": "fdb8cba1273830698d1a719dd7abc36031b21747e148d8620fe99ddabe3cd125",
  "duplicate_of": { "id": "01a1f133-2e26-7330-bebc-856e33e8b215", "outcome": "processed" },
  "handled_at": null,
  "outcome": null
}
```

- **Headers keep every value, with names in lower case,** in the order they came. Headers beginning `Tailscale-` aren't stored, since they name who on your tailnet sent the request.
- **Read until `next_cursor` is `null`.** A page holds 50 by default, and `limit` takes up to 200.
- **Only the connector's own key** reads deliveries. Any other key, the owner's included, is refused `403 forbidden`.

### Check the signature

Anyone who learns the address can post to it, so a stored delivery **proves nothing about who sent it**. Most vendors sign the body with a shared secret and send the signature in a header. [Get an inbound delivery's body](/reference/api/inbound-webhooks/getInboundDeliveryBody) answers the body byte for byte, as `application/octet-stream`:

```ts title="src/check.ts"
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

const { data: body } = await marfa.GET("/connectors/{id}/deliveries/{delivery_id}/body", {
  params: { path: { id: connectorId, delivery_id: delivery.id } },
  parseAs: "arrayBuffer",
});
const header = delivery.headers.find(([name]) => name === "x-signature")?.[1] ?? "";
const sent = /^sha256=[0-9a-f]{64}$/i.test(header) ? Buffer.from(header.slice(7), "hex") : Buffer.alloc(0);
const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(new Uint8Array(body!)).digest();
const genuine = sent.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(sent, expected);
```

Each vendor names its own header, prefix and encoding, so follow its documentation. Refuse a signature of the wrong shape, and compare in constant time. **Sign the bytes as they arrived**: parsing the body first changes them. A delivery that fails the check isn't the vendor's: read nothing from it and mark it `rejected`.

### Act on a delivery

Treat a delivery as **a prompt to read the vendor**, not as the vendor's state: vendors send webhooks out of order, twice, or not at all. Take from it only what names the thing that changed, such as a recipe's ID, then fetch that from the vendor and write it as [Pull from a vendor](/build/connector-pull) shows. **Keep the scheduled read**, for the webhook that never comes.

When a delivery repeats an earlier one's `duplicate_header` value on the same endpoint, Marfa stores both and sets the later one's `duplicate_of` to the earliest it still holds. If that one's `outcome` is `processed`, you've already acted on the change.

### Mark it handled

[Mark inbound deliveries handled](/reference/api/inbound-webhooks/markInboundDeliveriesHandled) takes 1 to 200 IDs and one outcome:

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
POST /connectors/01a1f12f-798c-70d4-b57b-d57feabdad99/deliveries/handled
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{ "ids": ["01a1f133-2e26-7330-bebc-856e33e8b215"], "outcome": "processed" }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.POST("/connectors/{id}/deliveries/handled", {
  params: { path: { id: connectorId } },
  body: { ids: ["01a1f133-2e26-7330-bebc-856e33e8b215"], outcome: "processed" },
});
```

- **`processed`:** you read the vendor because of the delivery, and the run succeeded.
- **`duplicate`:** an earlier delivery of the same change was processed.
- **`rejected`:** the delivery failed your check, or names nothing you act on.

**The first mark stands**: marking a delivery again leaves the mark it has. So mark one `processed` only after the run that used it ends without error. An unmarked delivery comes back in the next listing, so a failed run loses nothing.

### What the vendor is told

Marfa answers the vendor **before your connector sees anything**. Many vendors send a refused request again:

| Answer | When |
| --- | --- |
| `202`, with the delivery's `id` | Marfa stored the delivery. |
| `404 not_found` | The address isn't a live endpoint: it was retired, never existed, or its connector was deleted or its key revoked or expired. |
| `413 request_too_large` | The body is over 25 MiB, unless the owner set another `inbound_max_bytes`. |
| `408 request_timeout` | No byte of the body arrived for 30 seconds. |
| `429 rate_limited`, with `Retry-After` | The endpoint is past its request limit, 600 a window unless the owner set another. |
| `503 inbound_unavailable`, with `Retry-After` | The connector's backlog or retained limit, or the instance's limit on bytes received at once, is reached. |

Marfa stores nothing for a refused request. Unless the owner sets others, a connector's backlog of unhandled deliveries and the deliveries it retains, handled or not, are each limited to 10,000 deliveries and 1 GiB, and the instance receives at most 100 MiB at once. Marking a delivery handled frees its place in the backlog, but **only age removes it** from the retained count: after 7 days if handled and 30 if not, unless the owner [sets other windows](/run/settings#change-settings-while-it-runs). [Errors](/reference/errors) lists every refusal.

### Replace an endpoint

To move a vendor to another address, create an endpoint, give the vendor its path, and **retire the old one** once the vendor has switched. A registration holds at most 10 live endpoints, and an eleventh is refused `409 conflict`.

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa connectors endpoints retire 01a1f12f-798c-70d4-b57b-d57feabdad99 01a1f133-2dc4-75cf-84fd-eb21a8a270fe
```

```http tab="HTTP"
DELETE /connectors/01a1f12f-798c-70d4-b57b-d57feabdad99/endpoints/01a1f133-2dc4-75cf-84fd-eb21a8a270fe
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.DELETE("/connectors/{id}/endpoints/{endpoint_id}", {
  params: { path: { id: connectorId, endpoint_id: "01a1f133-2dc4-75cf-84fd-eb21a8a270fe" } },
});
```

[Retiring an endpoint](/reference/api/inbound-webhooks/retireInboundEndpoint) keeps it in the list with `retired_at` set. Its deliveries stay readable and **still count toward the limits**, so mark them as usual.

The rules behind this page are in the [inbound webhooks](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/inbound-webhooks.md) chapter of the contract.
